about.title: Los Alamitos Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Los Alamitos is a small city, but its roads carry a steady flow of traffic between Orange County and the I-605, and that traffic produces real consequences. Recent public records show 88 injury collisions in a single year, with 110 people hurt and one life lost — numbers that translate into real families dealing with pain, missed work, and mounting bills. Crashes here tend to cluster on Fridays during the late-afternoon commute, often along Katella Avenue, Los Alamitos Boulevard, and Cerritos Avenue, where cross-traffic and left turns create opportunities for collisions. If you were injured in one of these crashes, what happens in the days afterward matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured Los Alamitos residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the claim, deal with insurance adjusters, and help protect your right to recover for your losses.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Talk to an Insurer

items.title: The clock is already running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a lawsuit, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting early helps preserve options.

items.title: Fault doesn't have to be all-or-nothing
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly at fault — your share of responsibility simply reduces the amount, it doesn't eliminate your claim.

items.title: A recorded statement can work against you
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash; you're not required to give one, and an independent attorney can speak for you so your words aren't later used to minimize your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Los Alamitos?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government entity, such as the city or a public transit vehicle, was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth getting guidance quickly.

items.question: I was hurt on Katella Avenue during a Friday evening commute — does that matter for my claim?
items.answer: The time and location of a crash can help establish traffic patterns and evidence like signal timing or witness availability, which may support your version of events. An attorney can request relevant records before they're lost or overwritten.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you contributed to the crash. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not barred entirely.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost or obligation to find out where you stand.
